nginx_off_by_slash.description: Nginx proxy_pass off-by-slash — a missing trailing slash in proxy_pass lets the client traverse to other backend routes. location /api { proxy_pass http://backend; } means /api../admin reaches /admin on the backend.

probes.description: Path traversal via missing trailing slash — /api../admin resolves to /admin on backend
URL-encoded traversal — proxy may not decode before matching location
Semicolon path parameter traversal — Tomcat/Jetty treat ;x=y as a path param

x_rewrite_headers.description: Reverse proxy header override — X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL, X-Forwarded-Prefix to bypass path-based authentication. IIS/Nginx/Spring Cloud Gateway may route based on these headers instead of the real path.

probes.description: X-Original-URL bypass — IIS/ASP.NET routes on this header, ignoring the real request path
X-Rewrite-URL bypass — similar to X-Original-URL on some reverse proxies
X-Forwarded-Prefix bypass — Spring Cloud Gateway prepends this to the path before routing

path_normalization.description: Path normalization differences between proxy and backend — the proxy enforces /admin is 403, but the backend normalizes /./admin or /%2e/admin to /admin and serves 200.

probes.description: Dot-segment normalization — proxy sees /./admin (no match), backend normalizes to /admin
URL-encoded dot segment — proxy does not decode before matching
Null byte injection — some backends truncate at %00, serving /admin
Case sensitivity mismatch — proxy matches /admin (case-sensitive), backend serves /ADMIN (case-insensitive)
